page: Microsoft Azure E8ads_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Eadv6 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at a dedicated clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 472 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring 3080.38 and Geekbench single-core scoring 2101.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12321.11 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8317.0. Memory performance exhibits a notable tradeoff: while read-only cached small block memory bandwidth is average at 607.78 GB/sec, the uncached large block read-only memory bandwidth is weak at 37.68 GB/sec, placing in the bottom 25%.

The instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and text processing, supported by a strong Geekbench text processing score of 2711.0 and an average PassMark database operations score of 3876.73. It handles Redis SET operations at 11.53 million operations per second. However, due to the weak uncached large-block read bandwidth and a weak prompt processing speed of 23.66 tokens/sec for medium 7B LLM models, it is less optimal for massive-scale data streaming or larger machine learning inference tasks without GPU acceleration.
description: Microsoft Azure E8ads_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance powered by a dedicated 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 8 vCPUs, 4 physical cores, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a 472 GB NVMe SSD. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance delivers strong single-core CPU performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 3080.38 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2101.0. While multi-core and database operations perform at average levels, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 37.68 GB/sec. This configuration is highly suitable for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, and text processing workloads that benefit from its high memory-to-core ratio and fast local NVMe storage.
